summary: The Eco Experts' guide (updated 31 January 2024) breaks down UK solar panel costs: about £7,026 for a 3.5 kWp system on a three-bedroom house, with annual savings of around £537 and a 13.08-year break-even. It covers installation cost components, battery add-ons, savings via the Smart Export Guarantee, ways to cut costs (grants, group buying, finance), maintenance costs, and things to check before buying.
one_line: A 2024 UK guide to what solar panels cost by house size, what makes up installation prices, savings, break-even time, and ways to reduce costs.
key_facts: The average cost of buying and installing one 350W solar panel is £703, and solar panels cost about £2,007 per kWp in general.

A three-bedroom house typically needs a 3.5 kWp system of 10 panels costing £7,026; a 1-2 bedroom house needs 2.1 kWp (6 panels) at £4,216; a four or five-bedroom house needs 4.9 kWp (14 panels) at £9,837.
The cost of going solar has dropped by 82% since 2010, according to the International Renewable Agency (IRENA).
Solar panels cut electricity bills by 70% on average, saving a three-bedroom household about £537 a year, including £159 from Smart Export Guarantee (SEG) payments.
The average household breaks even in 13.08 years, leaving a 25-year profit of £6,405 for a three-bedroom house.
More than 1.4 million UK households have solar panels installed, according to the Microgeneration Certification Scheme (MCS).
The average solar battery for a three-bedroom house costs £4,500; batteries last around 12 years and add about 30% more usable solar energy but extend break-even by about a decade.
Installation costs split into materials (40-50%, £1,900-£4,400), business costs (30-40%, £1,500-£3,400) and labour (10-30%, £800-£2,000); installers mark up materials by around 30%.

Ways to reduce cost include the ECO4 scheme, Solar Together (saves 30-35%), the Home Energy Scotland Loan (interest free) and the Home Upgrade Grant; finance is offered by E.ON, Scottish Power, SolarStyle and Sunsave.
A replacement inverter costs £500-£1,000 since inverters last about 10 years versus 25-30 years for panels; professional cleaning costs about £100 and repairs range from £80 to £1,500.
A 3.5 kW solar roof tile system costs £14,550 on average, almost twice the price of a panel system of the same size; a 5 kW system costs £20,250.
Installation usually takes one to two days, up to four days for more than 14 panels; the guide recommends getting at least five quotes, as advised by installer Everyone's Energy.
